subtype: Rubbing hands and drumming at work [Mismatch]
passage:
Dear Naveen,

In Thursday's stand-up you asked why I keep drumming my fingers on the table. I wanted to explain before you decide I am bored. Sometimes I rub my hands together when I am excited about something coming, like the demo next week. Other times I drum when I am waiting and a bit impatient, and I honestly cannot always tell which one I am doing. On Thursday it was impatience, because the meeting was running long and I had a call to make. You did not deserve to feel ignored. If my hands look restless, please just ask me. I would much rather clear it up. 🙂

Farhan

qa.q: What did Naveen ask Farhan about?
qa.a: Naveen asked why Farhan keeps drumming fingers on the table.

qa.q: What did Farhan's drumming mean on Thursday, and what else can hand movements mean for Farhan?
qa.a: On Thursday it meant impatience because the meeting was running long. Farhan says rubbing the hands can mean excitement, so the same restless hands can carry different feelings.

qa.q: What does Farhan suggest for dealing with the hand habits?
qa.a: Farhan suggests that Naveen simply ask when the hands look restless, which clears up the meaning faster than guessing.

qa.q: How might Naveen have felt during the stand-up when Farhan drummed?
qa.a: Naveen may have felt ignored or judged as boring, which is why the question was asked.

grounding: Illustrates hand rubbing or finger drumming that can mean anticipation or impatience, where asking works better than guessing.

subtype: Rubbing hands and drumming at work [Mismatch]
passage: You know, Ankita, when I began working at the print shop, I was Francis, the quiet one. And my hands gave me away. I used to rub them together when a big order was arriving, and the boss thought I was greedy for the commission. I drummed on the counter when a customer took too long and one customer thought I was rude. Neither was true. The first was excitement, the second was just fidgeting because I was tired. My manager finally said, "Francis, what is with your hands?" and I explained. Now I tell people if I notice it. Asking is easier than guessing, for both sides, honestly. Do not decide, just ask. 😊

qa.q: Where did Francis work at the start?
qa.a: Francis worked at a print shop.

qa.q: What did the boss and the customer wrongly think of Francis, and what was Francis really feeling?
qa.a: The boss thought Francis was greedy for the commission and the customer thought Francis was rude. The truth was excitement for the first and tired fidgeting for the second.

qa.q: What did Francis do that helped?
qa.a: When the manager asked about the hands, Francis explained, and now tells people on noticing it.

qa.q: How might the customer have felt when Francis drummed on the counter?
qa.a: The customer probably felt hurried or ignored, since they took the drumming as rudeness.

grounding: Illustrates hand rubbing and drumming that can be anticipation or impatience, resolved by asking instead of guessing.
